transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Montclair CTO), Laura Chen (Head of Infra), Diego Alvarez (Security), Allyson Rhee (PM)

Summary: quick discovery focused on private VPC deployment options for Redwood Private. Customer is evaluating Private (VPC) vs Dedicated. Primary concerns: network connectivity (peering vs PrivateLink), egress IPs, cross-region constraints, KMS integration, audit logs and compliance.

Topics: onboarding, VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink vs direct peering, region availability (us-east-1 requirement), data residency, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2, next steps for POC.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'll kick us off, so today we want to understand your infra constraints for a private deployment of Redwood, uh Montclair?
00:07 Samir: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. quick context - we're building an internal agent platform for retail banking support, gotta keep customer data in our VPC, so private only, no public egress.
00:18 Laura: yeah and we also have strict region rules, basically everything has to stay in us-east-1 for now, maybe eventually a us-west-2 mirror but primary is us-east-1.
00:28 Priya: okay that's common. can you tell us your preferred connectivity model - are you open to VPC peering, or do you prefer PrivateLink/Interface endpoints? any transit gateway constraints?
00:40 Laura: we run on AWS with a central transit gateway and a mix of peering for some partners. security prefers PrivateLink for SaaS but for vendor-hosted infra we typically do VPC peering when we own both sides. since this is private deployment with Redwood in our VPC, peering might be easiest, but we need to confirm routing and overlapping CIDRs.
01:01 Diego: yeah, key point for us - no internet egress for payloads, logs can be pushed to our S3 but must go through VPC endpoints; also need to lock down egress IPs for any external calls from the runtime.
01:12 Jordan: got it. quick clarifying Q - when you say 'Redwood in our VPC' you mean private control plane where customer manages the network and we deploy the runtime into their AWS account? or you want Redwood to manage but peered into your VPC?
01:25 Samir: ideally we want customer-managed deployment in our account, either via CloudFormation or Terraform, so we have full network control. we want the control plane maybe in a separate management VPC but everything data-plane stays inside our account.
01:37 Priya: that aligns with Redwood Private - we support customer-managed VPC deployments where the runtime runs in your account. we can provide templates and an operator to spin up, or we can do a managed install into your VPC if needed. both have trade-offs.
01:49 Laura: what about service endpoints - do you require public endpoints for the management plane? we can't have anything with a public DNS.
01:56 Priya: management/control plane can be run in your account as well, or we can provide a private endpoint. our usual approach is to provision an internal ALB with interface endpoints or use PrivateLink for selective control plane APIs. there's also a variant where the control plane is hosted but all data is proxied through your VPC - depends on compliance.
02:12 Diego: KMS integration is big - we need to use our CMKs for model keys and for logs encryption, and ideally HSM-backed keys for the highest classification. can Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
02:25 Priya: yes we support customer KMS via IAM roles and policies; for HSM-backed CMKs you'd need to share the ARN and we use customer-managed encryption for storage. there are sometimes caveats for runtime keys in memory; we can limit plaintext key exposure and use envelope encryption.
02:40 Samir: okay. latency question - we're sensitive, low-latency requirements for inference on some routes. if we self-host in us-east-1 will latency be comparable to Redwood hosted? and how does dedicated vs private compare on cost?
02:56 Jordan: short answer: private and dedicated can be tuned for latency - dedicated is reserved capacity on Redwood-managed infra and offers SLA-backed latency; private gives you more network control and potentially lower intra-VPC latency but you manage autoscaling and capacity unless we provide reserved nodes in your account. cost will be higher for private since you carry infra costs, but you get data control.
03:17 Laura: on autoscaling - we have infra automation but need to know instance types recommended, GPU family, and whether you support quantized model runtimes that run on cheaper GPUs.
03:28 Priya: we provide recommended instance types per model; for quantized floats we have optimizations to run on T4/A10g equivalents. we'll share the model profile sheet. autoscaling is controlled via operator which hooks into cluster autoscaler; we can do spot/ondemand mix.
03:40 Allyson: timeline - if we sign, how quickly can we onboard private? we're hoping to start a POC next week and run a two-week benchmark.
03:48 Jordan: typical POC onboarding for private is 1-2 weeks for infra provisioning if everything's ready; we can accelerate if you share AWS account IDs and networking constraints today.
03:58 Laura: we'll get those. on network specifics - our VPC has overlapping address space with some partners, can we do NAT-based connectivity? also concerned about Security Groups and cross-account roles.
04:10 Priya: overlapping CIDR is a blocker for peering; PrivateLink does not require non-overlapping CIDR but needs ENIs and VPCEs. Another option is a transit gateway with NAT or an intermediary VPC. For cross-account roles, we use IAM cross-account assumption roles for install.
04:27 Diego: compliance - we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, S3 buckets with object lock for a 7-year retention for certain datasets, and we need to know how Redwood stores logs and access logs.
04:38 Jordan: we can configure runtime to send audit logs to your S3 via Kinesis or direct API. logs at rest can be encrypted with your CMK and lifecycle rules applied. we also provide audit events for model invocations, admin actions, and system events.
04:52 Priya: small note - some transcription is fuzzy, sorry, but we do capture the high-level.
05:00 Samir: okay on network egress IPs - can Redwood guarantee static egress IPs if runtime requires calling external services? we need allow lists for third-party partners.
05:12 Priya: if the runtime runs in your account you control egress via NAT Gateways or Egress-only NAT. if Redwood manages outbound, we can provide a static egress IP range via NAT in a managed transit account, but that would need to be scoped in the contract.
05:26 Laura: we'd prefer to own egress so we can lock it down.
05:29 Jordan: noted. Diego, about keys - any specific HSM vendor or just AWS CloudHSM?
05:35 Diego: AWS CloudHSM is preferred, but we also have a Thales HSM for some workloads. at minimum we want CMKs in KMS with HSM backing.
05:45 Priya: we can integrate with CloudHSM-backed CMKs. for external HSMs there may be additional steps. we'll document that.
05:54 Allyson: what about region constraints - you said us-east-1 only, does Redwood Private support single-region installs?
06:01 Jordan: yes, we can do single-region installs; our operator supports region-specific deployment. we do recommend a multi-AZ setup in that region. Cross-region replication for backups is optional but given your policy it can be disabled.
06:14 Samir: good. one more - branching on traffic: can we route production-critical traffic to a dedicated pool while devs use a cheaper private cluster? basically mix of dedicated/dyno?
06:26 Priya: yes we support routing policies. requests can be routed by model, route, or service tier. you could have a dedicated capacity pool for low-latency high-priority routes and cheaper private nodes for background tasks. we'll share config examples for route policies.
06:40 Laura: for the POC, we plan a test harness that sends 500 concurrent short-context requests, and also a second workload for long-context summarization. will Redwood provide a benchmarking template?
06:50 Priya: yes, we'll provide a benchmark plan and recommended test vectors. we'll include token accounting and expected throughput per instance.
07:00 Diego: security question - do you support SSO via SAML/Okta for admin access? and RBAC to limit who can trigger model rollouts?
07:09 Jordan: yes, SAML SSO is supported, Okta is common. RBAC is granular - roles for viewer, operator, admin, and playground access; we can map to your groups.
07:18 Samir: compliance paperwork - can you provide a SOC 2 report and ISO certs?
07:22 Jordan: yes we'll send SOC 2 Type II report and our security whitepaper. I've added that to next steps.
07:28 Allyson: any blockers for data residency? we need proof that logs and models won't be replicated outside the region during normal operations.
07:35 Priya: by default private installs keep data in-region; backups can be configured not to replicate. we'll document the storage patterns and backup policies.
07:45 Laura: what's the upgrade story - if Redwood pushes a runtime update, can we schedule maintenance windows? we need change control.
07:53 Priya: yes, upgrades are controlled via operator; we can perform canary rollouts and require maintenance windows. for managed installs we'll coordinate.
08:03 Diego: incident response - need to know contact process and on-call; SLAs for incident ack/mitigation?
08:10 Jordan: for enterprise tiers we have 24/7 on-call with specified SLAs; we'll include a summary of response times in the package.
08:18 Samir: pricing ballpark - we want to understand infra cost plus Redwood license.
08:23 Jordan: we'll send a pricing sheet. private has infra + license; dedicated is license + reserved capacity. I'll include sample TCO scenarios based on your concurrency profiles.
08:33 Laura: small nit - we require VPC flow logs to be delivered to our logging account. can Redwood forward or do we need to enable flow logs in our VPC?
08:41 Priya: you should enable VPC Flow Logs in your account; we can also push agent-side logs to your endpoints. we'll include a checklist of which logs to enable.
08:50 Allyson: for the POC acceptance criteria - low-latency 95th percentile under X ms, token throughput > Y tps, and quality thresholds on a set of prompts. can we align on those?
08:59 Jordan: yes we'll draft the POC acceptance criteria. Priya: we'll own measurement and provide dashboards.
09:07 Samir: any gotchas with PrivateLink? we've had trouble with limits on ENIs in high throughput scenarios.
09:14 Priya: good point - PrivateLink scales with NLB+ENI capacity; for high throughput we sometimes recommend peering with a transit gateway or using dedicated instances in your account. we'll include guidance.
09:25 Laura: also need to know required IAM permissions for the install; we want a minimal privileges list.
09:31 Priya: we'll provide a least-privilege IAM template.
09:36 Diego: on egress auditing - we need logs of all external network calls from the runtime, not just successful ones. can Redwood capture that?
09:44 Priya: yes, runtime can emit network call events; we'll need sidecar-level logging enabled and permissions to write to your logging S3 or Kinesis.
09:54 Jordan: ok let's recap quick and call out next steps.
09:57 Jordan: recap - Montclair wants a customer-managed private deployment in us-east-1, strict no-public-data egress, CloudHSM-backed CMKs, VPC peering preferred but open to PrivateLink if CIDR overlaps, require audit logs to our SIEM and S3 with retention, and POC next week. action items: Jordan to send security docs and diagram, Priya to prepare benchmark plan, Laura to share account IDs and networking constraints, Diego to review KMS/HSM notes.
10:20 Samir: that's it, thanks everyone. we'll look for the docs and target to have AWS details by Monday.
10:26 Jordan: perfect, thanks - we'll follow up with calendar invites for the POC kickoff.
10:30 End of recording.
